transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-14
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~74 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (CEO), Omar Haddad (CTO), Linda Becker (VP Product), Noah Chen (CFO), Priya Desai (Head of People), plus company-wide attendees (multiple)

Auto-generated summary:
CEO overview of late Q3/Q4 priorities; product deep-dive into M2 runtime improvements and customer-facing features; hiring update and org restructure for infra; short finance update on runway and reserved capacity uptake; SOC2/compliance recap; Q&A and open mic for employees.

Topics covered:
- Product: M1 -> M2 runtime changes, latency wins, quantization options
- Infrastructure: Dedicated clusters, private deployment adoption signals
- People: hiring priorities, comp adjustments, manager training
- Finance: ARR cadence, reserved capacity traction, runway
- Security: SOC2 status and next steps

Transcript body:
[00:00:05] Maya: hey everyone, uh sorry for the slight delay, we were finishing up a few slides. super excited to get started, we have about, what, an hour and change? um so i'll kick off with a quick company pulse then we'll hand to linda and omar for product and infra, and then noah and priya will close.

[00:00:28] (applause emoji in chat)

[00:00:32] Maya: big picture — we're seeing really solid customer momentum in the last quarter. reserved capacity deals are up, and the feedback that i've been hearing is that customers love the predictable throughput, and, and — this is important — they're asking for clearer rollout paths to private deployments. so, our thesis about serving over model ownership is paying off but it's also bringing new operational asks.

[00:01:05] Maya: quick numbers: MMR (monthly?) — mmr... monthly recurring revenue, sorry — is up about 28% q/q in paid accounts using dedicated, and hosted API still growing in low double digits. overall runway is healthy. noah will give the specifics in a minute.

[00:01:25] Linda: thanks, maya. hi all. product update — we're focused on three things for Q4: 1) Latency corridors (meaning consistent p95 improvements), 2) M2 runtime feature set (kernel selection, continuous batching), and 3) developer ergonomics (better SDK docs and examples for private deploy).

[00:01:50] Linda: on latency — small wins: kernel pinning reduced p95 by about 18% on our internal 4k tests, but — and this is important — that number varies by model family and sequence distribution. also we've started an experiment with prefix caching heuristics on customers with repetitive prompts, and early numbers look like a 22% token-savings on chat workloads. these are internal and noisy, but promising.

[00:02:25] Speaker 1: (inaudible) are those numbers public anywhere?

[00:02:28] Linda: not publicly yet, we have a deck i'll share after the call. we'll also put an internal bench sheet with the raw runs — note these are on rtx sort of hardware in dedicated pools so cloud variability applies.

[00:02:40] Omar: hey folks — quick infra update. kernel work is moving faster than expected. we've got a branch that does dynamic kernel selection at runtime based on sequence histogram; it reduces wasted cycles when batch sizes tilt. this is not GA but it's in canary on two of our internal clusters.

[00:03:10] Omar: on private — we've seen three SOC2-driven POCs start this month where customers test the private control plane + KMS integration. the ask: better audit log granularity and SSO provisioning automation (saml/okta). engineering and security are pairing on that.

[00:03:34] (crosstalk; someone mentions 'KMS' and 'HSM')

[00:03:45] Maya: quick note on channels — if you're working on private deploy features, please sync with security early, there's a handful of product decisions that change the compliance posture.

[00:03:58] Noah: finance quick update — as maya said revenue is trending up. our committed reserved capacity bookings this quarter are 1.8x prior quarter; gross margin improved slightly due to better GPU utilization and some vendor rebates. runway is still north of 14 months at current burn assumptions. the main risk is if growth slows in hosted and dedicated renewals don't come through — which is why the sales motion and pricing trials matter.

[00:04:30] Noah: question from slack — "any update on enterprise discounting cadence?" short answer: we're tightening guardrails. deals that need deeper discounts need executive approval and tie to committed usage. we want to protect unit economics.

[00:04:52] Priya: hi everyone, people update — hiring is a top priority. we approved headcount for infra kernel team + two production ML engineers + one enterprise security PM. referral bonuses are extended for these roles; i'll post specifics. also rolling out a manager training series for new managers to standardize onboarding.

[00:05:17] Priya: on org design — small change: infra will have a dedicated 'runtime performance' pod reporting to omar to reduce cross-team coordination overhead. rationale: we want faster kernel iterations without gating on infra ops schedule.

[00:05:36] (some 'cool' and 'nice' in chat)

[00:05:45] Maya: ok, now open q&a — please keep questions short, and we may follow up offline.

[00:05:50] Daniel Park (Eng): hi — quick question on the caching heuristics — are we planning to make that configurable per-tenant? some tenants have different prompt repetition characteristics.

[00:06:02] Linda: yes, good point. the plan is: default heuristics enabled, with a toggle and tiered config for enterprise so they can modify expiry and prefix thresholds. working on the API spec now.

[00:06:18] Sofia Liu (ML): follow-up — what about quality regression alerts when we change quantization profiles? we don't want customers to silently degrade.

[00:06:28] Linda: agreed, that's in the Optimize playbook. we'll tie quantization rollouts to eval sets and automated quality checks; product will require a fallback policy to earlier float variants.

[00:06:38] Omar: i'll add that to the kernel office hours and we can walk through a rollout checklist.

[00:06:45] Karim (Sales): question for noah — any change to pricing for prepay reserved pools? we have a few customers asking about flexible monthly commits.

[00:06:55] Noah: we're piloting a 'monthly reserved' price with slightly higher rate vs annual but much lower vs on-demand. it's aimed at mid-market customers who can't commit annually. sales should route prospective customers to finance-subsidized pilots first. details in the pricing doc.

[00:07:10] (longer pause while Maya reads chat)

[00:07:20] Maya: other big announcement — we are formalizing an internal innovation budget. each team can propose a two-week sprint for kernel or model experiments with a small budget for bench time and dedicated infra. winners get follow-on engineering time. more details in the #innovation channel.

[00:07:40] (applause)

[00:07:45] Maya: also, small people note — for comp cycles, managers should calibrate within bands; people ops will publish guidance. we've seen some outliers and want to ensure fairness.

[00:07:58] Priya: yes, banding doc coming. and one ask — managers please finalize performance calibration by Oct 31.

[00:08:10] (questions from remote offices about timezone AMA sessions)

[00:08:22] Maya: we'll host two follow-up AMAs, one for APAC and one for Americas. sign-up sheet in the invite follow-up.

[00:08:30] (someone asks a light-hearted question about "will we get hoodies?")

[00:08:34] Maya: hoodies — maybe for the innovation sprint winners.

--- mid-call product deep-dive ---
[00:30:05] Linda: ok deep-dive — M2 runtime specifics. the big change is that we're moving to a more modular kernel architecture to support BYOK quantization layers. this will let us ship quantized variants without large model rewrites. consequence: slightly more build-time complexity but much faster runtime rollout.

[00:30:35] Linda: demo note: we had an internal demo where a 6.7b open model moved from fp16 to int8 with a 2.1x throughput improvement and <3% quality delta on our selected eval sets. caveat: others have seen different deltas depending on prompt distributions.

[00:31:02] Omar: technical caveat — int8 paths require careful attention to KV cache memory layout. we documented a migration path for active sessions but it is somewhat brittle; that's why kernel office hours are important.

[00:31:25] Speaker 2: are we planning to open-source any of the kernel tooling?

[00:31:28] Omar: no immediate plan, at least until we fully validate on private customer fleets. after that we may open-source smaller helper libs.

[00:31:40] (noise — someone drops off the call briefly)

[00:50:12] Maya: quick lightning round — wins from the field, callouts. karim, any customer stories?

[00:50:17] Karim (Sales): quick one — a fintech customer moved a beta from on-prem to our dedicated pool and reported a 30% reduction in tail latency and liked the clearer billing. they're now evaluating a private deployment for compliance.

[00:50:30] Elena (Support): we had a spike in tickets around SSO and session timeouts; engineering pushed a config fix yesterday that resolved most cases.

[00:50:42] Maya: awesome. ok near the end, i'm going to recap and then we will close with open mic for 10 minutes.

[00:50:55] Maya: recap: 1) product: M2 kernel + caching work continues; expect a roadmap deck; 2) infra: kernel office hours + private deploy POCs; 3) people: hiring approvals and manager training; 4) finance: reserved capacity growth and tightened discounting guardrails; 5) security: SOC2 timeline with outstanding items — noah will share.

[00:51:25] (someone types 'thanks' in chat)

[00:51:30] Maya: before we go open mic, a reminder — if you have a question that is sensitive, drop it into the anonymous form in #company-ops and we'll triage.

Open mic / Q&A:
[00:51:50] (various quick comments, laughter, shoutouts for new hires)

[00:58:22] Employee (anonymous): can we get more clarity on leveling and individual IC growth paths?

[00:58:35] Priya: great ask — people ops will schedule a leveling doc walkthrough and AMA next week. we'll also publish career ladders for ic and manager paths.

[00:59:10] Employee: are there plans for any new office hubs?

[00:59:18] Maya: short answer: yes, exploratory conversations for a small APAC hub, nothing finalized.

[01:01:12] (end of questions; final thanks)

[01:01:20] Maya: thanks everyone for joining. please look out for follow-ups in email and in the #all-hands follow-up thread.

Action items recap (auto):
- Priya: publish hiring priorities + referral details (due 2025-10-21)
- Linda: share product roadmap deck + bench sheet (due 2025-10-17)
